newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end little changed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end little changed in thin trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed in thin trade on Tuesday, with the Canadian market taking direction from U.S. Treasuries amid a lack of Canadian economic data, analysts said.
"I wouldn't say there's too much specifically Canadian that is driving this. I think we've mostly taken our lead from the U.S.," said Arve Bendiksrud, fixed-income analyst with TD Securities.
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 traded unchanged at C$100.82 to yield 7.924 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 21/32 to yield 7.06 percent.
The spread between benchmark bonds widened to 86 basis points from 81 basis points near the close of trading on Friday.

Canadian and U.S. bond markets opened sharply lower this morning after a press report said the U.S. Federal Reserve is willing to hike U.S. rates by 50 basis points if the economy does not show signs of slowing down, analysts said.

Both markets later pared losses as an economic report showed U.S. retail sales rose just 0.8 percent in the four weeks of fiscal August versus July. The number helped to calm investor fears that the U.S. economy may be overheating.
Canada may be underperforming U.S. issues as some investors take profits on the recent narrowing in Canada-U.S. long bond spreads, said Bendiksrud.
Investors in Canadian bonds are also looking ahead to Wednesday, when the Government of Canada auctions C$3.0 billion of 6.25 percent bonds due September 15, 1998.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.08 to C$96.63 to yield 7.475 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 11/32 to yield 6.90 percent.
The spread between the two bonds widened to 58 basis points from 52 basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 4.10 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.32 percent.
